page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB per virtual processor. The underlying x86_64 CPU architecture includes vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware cryptographic capabilities including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for persistence.

Empirical benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread computational capacity. Stress-ng single-core tests score 3115.19, placing the instance in the top 10 percent of recorded systems, while Geekbench single-core reaches 2028.0. Multi-core performance sits within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud servers, registering 24940.13 in stress-ng and 12205.0 in Geekbench. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 49.71 GB/sec alongside write bandwidth of 27.96 GB/sec, backed by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Baseline networking bandwidth is rated at 12 Gbps.

By omitting dedicated hardware accelerators and local solid-state drives, ecs.c8ae.4xlarge focuses physical resources entirely on CPU execution and networking. This design suits CPU-intensive workloads that require dependable single-core performance without requiring excessive memory footprints, including software compilation, text processing, CI/CD pipelines, and distributed web serving tiers.
